q: What is the core principle of IFRS 15?
a: Revenue is recognised to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to a customer, in an amount reflecting the consideration the entity expects to be entitled to.

q: How does IFRS 15 define control of an asset?
a: The ability to direct the use of the asset and obtain substantially all of its remaining benefits.

q: List the five steps of IFRS 15.
a: 1 Identify the contract. 2 Identify the performance obligations. 3 Determine the transaction price. 4 Allocate the price. 5 Recognise revenue when (or as) each obligation is satisfied.

q: What conditions must a contract meet to be within IFRS 15?
a: Approved and committed; rights identifiable; payment terms identifiable; commercial substance; collection probable.

q: When is a promised good or service distinct?
a: The customer can benefit from it on its own (or with readily available resources) AND it is separately identifiable from other promises in the contract.

q: When is variable consideration included in the transaction price?
a: Only if it is highly probable that a significant reversal of revenue will not occur when the uncertainty is resolved.

q: How is the transaction price allocated?
a: In proportion to the stand-alone selling prices of each performance obligation (estimated if not sold separately).

q: When is revenue recognised over time?
a: If the customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefit; or the work creates/enhances an asset the customer controls; or no alternative-use asset is created and the entity has an enforceable right to payment to date.

q: Name the indicators that control has passed at a point in time.
a: Present right to payment; legal title; physical possession; risks and rewards transferred; customer acceptance.
Output: value to the customer of what was transferred (surveys, units delivered). Input: entity's inputs (labour hours, costs incurred).
Principal controls the goods first and records gross revenue. Agent arranges the supply and records only its fee or commission.

q: Forward or call option with repurchase price at or above the sale price?
a: No control transfer. Financing arrangement: keep the asset, recognise a liability, difference is interest. If the price is below the sale price: lease (IFRS 16).

q: What must all be true for control to pass in a bill-and-hold sale?
a: Substantive reason; goods separately identified as the customer's; ready for transfer; entity cannot use them or send them to another customer.

q: Contract asset, receivable, contract liability: what differs?
a: Contract asset: performed, right to payment conditional on more than time. Receivable: unconditional, only time. Contract liability: paid or due before performance.

q: How is a sale with a right of return recorded?
a: No revenue for goods expected back. Refund liability, reduce revenue, and an asset for the right to recover the goods (adjusted against cost of sales).

q: How is a warranty that is required by law and not sold separately treated?
a: Not a performance obligation. Account for it under IAS 37.
